Manurangsi–Sornat 2026 arxiv:2604.05953 full primary Theorem 5, Corollary 9
correctness.rationale: Let M(k) be maximum covered voters by exactly k approval candidates. Before all voters in the union U are covered, each optimal committee can add a strictly new voter; increments are positive integers, with M(2)-M(1)<=M(1). For <=3 candidates, submodularity of coverage shows 2M(2)>=M(1)+M(3). For arbitrary candidates with <=5 voters, any first strict convex step at k>=3 forces maximum supporter-set size <=1; at k=2, max set size <=2 and the three-set union estimate excludes M(1)=2,M(2)=3,M(3)>=5. For six voters and four candidates, violation at k=3 would require at least 8 private vertices among 6, impossible; at k=2 integer constraints force (M1,M2,M3)=(3,4,6). An optimal covering triple has three disjoint two-element supports; the fourth is a 3-element transversal, giving profile 0,3,4,6,6. Exactly 6!/(2!^3 3!)×2^3=120 voter-labelled candidate-unlabelled profiles, 2880 fully labelled. Explicit voter orderings after deletion establish voter-deletion criticality for consecutive-ones domain. Independent enumeration of every 4-multiset of subsets of n labelled voters n=3,4,5,6 found no violations for n<6 and exactly 120 canonical cases for n=6. This does not substitute for the arbitrary-number-of-candidates proof.

evidence: The full 30-page Manurangsi–Sornat article proves concavity under the voter-interval hypothesis for broader Thiele rules.
Classical maximum coverage and submodularity yield marginal diminishing returns for a fixed set but not necessarily concavity of optimal k-set values.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A stronger result on interval profiles is inapplicable because the counterexample has no interval ordering. General submodularity of the set function cannot be converted into global concavity of its optimal size-k envelope; the explicit six-voter example disproves that putative implication.
